caption: The drawing depicts two dark, metallic-looking silhouettes against a light beige background. At the top left of the central rectangular area is a hanging sign with a curled bracket supporting a horizontal bar. The sign, shaped like an arrow with a directional point on the right, reads "JACOB ISET" on the first line and "ANO 1764" on the second line, both in a cutout style that allows the background to show through the letters. Below and to the right, there is a weather vane or figure of a person in a broad-brimmed hat sitting upright on a horse, with the person’s right arm extended and pointing forward. The horse is standing with its head facing left and its tail curved downward. Both the sign and the horse-and-rider figure are rendered in solid, textured dark brown or black color. Subtle, thin, curved lines form decorative arcs throughout the background of the central rectangular area. At the bottom of the drawing, just below the rectangle, are the words "ONE-SIXTH ACTUAL SIZE" and "ELMER G. ANDERSON" in small, light gray text. The entire design is centered on a blank, off-white sheet.
title: Two Weather Vanes
